brief: Goldman Sachs estimates hyperscalers need roughly $300bn in annual AI revenues within the next few years to break even on 2026-2027 capex, which implies AI users would need to spend roughly $1 trillion annually on AI applications for hyperscalers to earn solid returns and the application layer to hold strong margins. That compares with $1.5 trillion in global 2026 software spending and $1.8 trillion in potential annual US labor productivity gains GS economists expect to eventually accrue to capital, though not all of that would flow to the infrastructure or application layers; physical AI or AGI would raise both figures further. Within the AI trade, data infrastructure and cybersecurity stocks have recently outperformed while consumer inertia names have underperformed. Separately, GS introduces a framework requiring the six major US hyperscalers to generate a combined ~$1.42 trillion in cumulative 2028-2030 revenue (~$11.6bn per GW) to clear a 15% ROIC hurdle on 2026-2027 AI-compute capex, framing near-term return compression as a function of the investment cycle rather than poor AI economics, and still sees a solid return profile for capital deployed over the next 18 months against a 3-5 year opportunity.
